# Psalm 56 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the music director. To the tune of 'A Dove on Distant Oaks.' A psalm of David, regarding the time the Philistines seized him in Gath.

**2** O God, have mercy on me, for people are hounding me. My foes attack me all day long.

**3** I am constantly hounded by those who slander me, and many are boldly attacking me.

**4** But when I am afraid, I will put my trust in You.

**5** I praise God for what He has promised. I trust in God, so why should I be afraid? What can mere mortals do to me?

**6** They are always twisting what I say; they spend their every waking moment plotting to harm me.

**7** They conspire together, lurking in wait, watching my every move, eager to kill me.

**8** Don't let them get away with their wickedness; in Your anger, O God, bring them down.

**9** You keep track of all my sorrows. You have collected all my tears in Your bottle. You have recorded each one in Your book.

**10** My enemies will retreat when I call to You for help. This one thing I know: God is on my side!

**11** I praise God for what He has promised; yes, I praise the LORD for what He has promised.

**12** I trust in God, so why should I be afraid? What can mere mortals do to me?

**13** I will fulfill my vows to You, O God, and will offer a sacrifice of thanks for Your help.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **56:5**: 'What can flesh do to me?' — Hebrews 13:6 echoes this. The contrast between mortal threat and divine power reduces human danger to insignificance.

— PNEUMA
